answer: Each request enters a rolling behavior graph. When keys repeat timing, task order and payout destination within a window, the gateway merges their quotas and keeps one shared cap until activity diverges. Proposed graph-screening cost is 0.04 credits per identity: 1,000 fake keys × 0.04 = 40 credits of analysis, versus 0.04 for one honest agent once. Like bees following nectar, a thread of matching calls reveals a swarm; ferrous filings around a magnet show how correlated keys cluster. This can wrongly merge honest agents with similar workflows.
